problem.title: Publishing more does not answer the right questions
problem.body: Content becomes difficult to manage when topics overlap, pages lack a defined audience, or useful evidence is buried under broad language. Search visibility needs a connected editorial system, not a larger pile of pages.

method.title: Plan useful coverage around real audience questions
method.intro: The work connects demand, expertise, page purpose, and distribution so each content decision has a reason to exist.

steps.title: Audience questions
steps.body: Group the questions, decisions, and objections that matter to the audience, then distinguish a useful topic from a superficial keyword variation.

steps.title: Topic architecture
steps.body: Assign topics to hubs, supporting pages, and existing URLs so coverage grows without creating avoidable overlap or orphaned work.

steps.title: Evidence and usefulness
steps.body: Set expectations for first-hand detail, sources, examples, structure, and editorial review before a page is drafted or refreshed.

steps.title: Search and AI discovery
steps.body: Structure clear answers and supporting context so content is easier to interpret across conventional search and AI-search surfaces, without treating GEO as a separate service.

outcome.title: A content roadmap with a reason behind every page
outcome.body: The roadmap gives writers, editors, and site owners a shared basis for deciding what to create, improve, connect, and eventually retire.
points: Topics tied to audience needs and business priorities
Clear relationships between hub and supporting pages
Editorial requirements that protect usefulness and trust
Content structured for clear answers and supporting context
